sources.entry: Kopi - Local-first clipboard manager with searchable history, pinboards and plain-text paste. Skips password manager copies.

summary.one_liner: Kopi is an open-source, local-first clipboard manager for macOS and Windows with searchable history, pinboards, snippets and optional local-network sync.
summary.what_it_does: Kopi records everything you copy (text, rich text, links, images, files, colors and code) and tags each clip with the app it came from. You can search history as you type, filter by kind or app, preview clips, and paste with Return, as plain text with ⌥Return, or with ⌘1–9 on macOS. Pins and pinboards keep reused clips, and snippets can be pasted with a keystroke, including the date or a blank to fill in. It reads text inside copied images on the machine so that text is searchable, and it skips copies from password managers and concealed content. History limits by count, age and size keep pinned clips. Sync between Macs and PCs runs directly over the local network, end-to-end encrypted, with no server, and is off until enabled.
use_cases: Clipboard history across Mac and Windows
Keep clipboard data private and offline
Sync clipboard between my computers on the local network
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash (macOS quick install script, as given in README; URL is blank in the README)
Or download Kopi_ _universal.dmg from the newest GitHub release and drag Kopi to Applications (macOS 14+)
Or download Kopi_ _x64-setup.exe from the newest release and run it (Windows 10/11, 64-bit)
git clone the repository, then cd kopi
pnpm dev:desktop (run in development) or pnpm build:desktop (builds Kopi.app)
notable: Cross-platform with the same shortcuts and history on macOS and Windows
Local-first: no account, works offline, history stays on the computer
Serverless end-to-end encrypted sync over the local network
On-device text recognition in copied images for search
Privacy filter skips password manager and concealed copies
caveats: Alpha quality on macOS and Windows; Windows is the newest and has the most rough edges
Not notarized on macOS, so Gatekeeper must be bypassed on first launch; Windows installer is unsigned
Sync is listed as working only over the local network; cross-network sync is not described
